title: Tubig Pilipinas secures up to P900-million investment from Maharlika
summary: The transaction is expected to give MIC a 9.9% ownership stake in Tubig Pilipinas if it invests the full P900 million

blocks.text: The transaction is expected to give MIC a 9.9% ownership stake in Tubig Pilipinas if it invests the full P900 million
MANILA, Philippines – Sovereign wealth fund Maharlika Investment Corporation (MIC) is investing up to P900 million in water utilities firm Tubig Pilipinas Holdings Inc.

MIC signed a convertible note agreement with Tubig Pilipinas on Friday, November 20, with an initial investment of P450 million. It comes with an option to put in another P450 million through a follow-on offering targeted for the first quarter of 2027.
The transaction is expected to give MIC a 9.9% ownership stake in Tubig Pilipinas if it invests the full P900 million.
According to its Philippine Stock Exchange disclosure, the funding will be used to “accelerate water infrastructure expansion,” particularly in underserved communities.

In a separate statement, MIC confirmed the agreement, with its outgoing president and chief executive Rafael “Joel” Consing Jr. describing the investment as part of the sovereign wealth fund’s strategy related to infrastructure.

“This partnership fits a deliberate pattern. Power for the islands. New port cities. Now, water. Power and water are what every community needs to function; ports are what connect them to growth,” Consing said.

blocks.caption: The Maharlika fund that Joel Consing leaves behind

blocks.text: Tubig Pilipinas operates water supply and distribution projects outside major metropolitan areas through its operating subsidiary, Tubig Pilipinas Group. Its portfolio includes water supply projects in Bacolod City, Negros Occidental, and water distribution systems in Trece Martires, Cavite; San Jose City, Nueva Ecija; Coron, Palawan; and Catbalogan, Samar.

The company itself is relatively new to the stock market in its present form, having completed a backdoor listing by acquiring the dormant Coal Asia Holdings earlier this year and rebranded it into TUBIG.
Its shares, however, have been suspended from trading since October 19 after a share-swap transaction reduced its public float to 10.64%, below the PSE’s 20% minimum requirement.
The Maharlika deal also comes just days before Consing’s term ends on November 23.
Consing earlier told reporters that MIC was working on two or three additional investments that could be announced before the end of 2026.

Since its establishment in 2023, Maharlika has invested in port operator Asian Terminals Inc., electricity-grid holding firm Synergy Grid and Development Philippines, and short-term financing for Petron, among others.

Still, the sovereign wealth fund has been exceedingly cautious in deploying its capital. As of end-September 2026, it had invested P24.7 billion, about a third of its initial P75 billion, while retaining P53.67 billion in cash and cash equivalents. – Rappler.com
